newsitem.title: USA: Brooks Fiber building two more networks.
newsitem.headline: Brooks Fiber building two more networks.

text.p: Brooks Fiber Properties Inc said Monday it will invest about $66 million to develop fiber optic networks in the Minneapolis/St. Paul market and the Long Island, N.Y., metropolitan area.
Brooks Fiber, which provides local telecommunications services, said the funds necessary to construct both markets are available from current cash balances.
The new networks will operate under the name Brooks Fiber Communications and will compete with the services of the local incumbent provider.
The networks will bring to 36 the number of cities in operation or under construction by Brooks Fiber. Its goal is to be in 40 cities by the end of 1997.

"These markets represent a significant increase in our addressable market potential, to approximately $21 billion for 36 markets from approximately $15 billion in our existing 33 markets," James Allen, vice-chairman and chief executive officer of Brooks Fiber Properties, said in a statement.

"While these are much larger markets than we have traditionally pursued, the operating agreements with certain of our strategic carrier customers will allow us to establish a significant position in each of these markets in a relatively short period of time," he added.
Construction of the networks will begin as soon as all permits are obtained, with services expected to be offered by the end of 1997.
